newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's king says Israel's building risks peace.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king says Israel's building risks peace.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein said in an interview published on Friday that Israel's decision to build a new Jewish settlement on an Arab East Jerusalem hilltop endangered the Middle East peace process.

The king was quoted by Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth as also saying that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had to expect opposition to the decision even if he had forewarned Arab leaders it would be taken.
Israel's decided on Wedensday to approve building 6,500 homes for Jews at the site Israel calls Har Homa and Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.
"A decision of this kind could endanger all that we have accomplished (in the peace process) up to now," the king was quoted by Yedioth as saying.
"On both sides live proud people. They should not be taunted or humiliated, in particular when peace contacts are being conducted with the other side which has large expectations of the peace."
The king held three hours of talks with Netanyahu in Amman on Sunday. Officials said the Jerusalem building project loomed large in the meeting.
"The side taking decisions must be prepared for reactions against them. It cannot be thought that only because we were informed beforehand...these projects are accepted by us."

Jordanian state television said on Wednesday that King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab ally since the two countries signed a 1994 peace treaty, sent a special envoy to warn Netanyahu of the gravity of the move.
